newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply off as back contracts.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply off as back contracts.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply lower after the yawning backwardation in London contracted swiftly on Wednesday when LME warned it was monitoring closely how the spreads evolved.

The LME's shot across the bow of a seemingly buoyant red metal ship was enough to send ripples of nervousness through the market, prompting a selloff which accelerated after stops were hit, traders said.
"The mood has changed very quickly, with a lot of long liquidation now going on," Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
The backwardation is high because of tightness in nearby LME dates to mid-February.

"The perception is, more and more, that this is a very short-term tightness," a trader said. The drop on Wednesday was too quick to see if consumers will now come in to buy and thereby support the market.
Most active March COMEX went out 3.65 cents weaker at 102.50 cents per pound, traded 105.30 to 101.70 cents.
The LME cash to three months spread or backwardation fell to $245/$255, off $80 to $90 from Tuesday's high, but the backwardation in the very close dates was still very high.
Volume on COMEX was estimated at 12,500 lots compared to Tuesday's 6,040 lots.
The first quarter of the year is normally the time of heaviest demand in the United States and the physical market is still healthy and fairly tight, traders said.

RTZ Corp's new smelter at Kennecott Utah Copper has been plagued by start up problems which partly caused the tightness on the U.S. market. RTZ said on Wednesday that Kennecott's converting furnace was still only operating at 51 percent of capacity by the end of the fourth quarter.
Meanwhile Chilean copper producer Enami has agreed a new five-year labor deal, removing a possible supply disruption.
Korea's LG Metals also said it had not requested increased credit lines nor had it received margin calls for its short positions on LME.
Many in market were worried over how LG would handle its short positions in the nearby tight dates on LME.
In announcing its fourth quarter results, ASARCO Inc said copper supply and demand were in balance and inventories at their lowest levels since mid-1990.
"At the same time, these favorable fundamentals appear to be replacing speculation as the primary influence in the copper market," ASARCO's Chairman Richard de J Osborne said.
